nodes.content: Develop reinforcement learning transfer for robotic manipulation that reuses skills under hidden dynamics shifts while limiting negative transfer.
requirements: Match from-scratch success rates using 50% fewer target interactions when manipulation dynamics partially overlap.
On incompatible targets, stay within 5 percentage points of from-scratch success under equal interaction budgets.

nodes.content: Reuse source skills through latent-dynamics adapters only when confidence-bounded target-rollout advantage exceeds a concurrently trained scratch policy; otherwise use scratch.
How reliably can limited target rollouts distinguish source skills worth adapting from skills that underperform scratch training?
Forty paired target rollouts let bootstrap-bound gating select helpful skills with ≥80% precision and reject harmful skills with ≥90% recall.
On 30-seed ManipShift, evaluate 40-rollout bootstrap gating using helpful-skill precision and harmful-skill recall versus scratch outcomes.
On 30-seed ManipShift, 40-rollout gating achieved 72% helpful-skill precision and 78% harmful-skill recall, below hypothesized 80%/90%.
Dynamics-stratified bootstrap gating with up to 80 paired target rollouts achieves ≥80% helpful-skill precision and ≥90% harmful-skill recall.
Using ManipShift’s 40-rollout gating errors, test 80-rollout dynamics-stratified bootstrap on held-out seeds for helpful-skill precision and harmful-skill recall.
On 30 held-out ManipShift seeds, 80-rollout stratified gating achieved 84% helpful-skill precision and 92% harmful-skill recall.
Replace the underperforming 40-rollout gate with 80-rollout dynamics-stratified gating; held-out precision and recall exceed 80%/90% thresholds.
ManipShift-40 audit table records 30-seed rollout scores, bootstrap gate decisions, scratch comparisons, and helpful/harmful skill labels.
Using adopted 80-rollout gate, test ManipShift overlap at half-budget success parity and incompatibility at equal-budget ≤5-point scratch gap.
Using ManipShift-40 audit labels, evaluate the 80-rollout gate across 30 seeds: overlap at half-budget; incompatibility at equal-budget versus scratch.
ManipShift transfer scorecard contains 30-seed success curves, target-interaction counts, scratch baselines, and overlap/incompatibility comparisons.
Route skills using latent transition fingerprints; disable incompatible primitives via conformal mismatch tests and train a target-specific residual policy.
Calibrate conformal fingerprint routing, train residual policies, and benchmark ManipShift half-budget overlap and equal-budget incompatible success against scratch.
Using ManipShift-40 audit labels, compare conformal fingerprint-routed residuals against bootstrap-gated adapters on half-budget overlap and equal-budget incompatible success.
On ManipShift, fingerprint routing achieved 61% half-budget overlap success versus 72% full-budget scratch; incompatible success trailed scratch by 9 points.
Does contact-phase fingerprint aliasing or residual-policy interference drive fingerprint routing’s 9-point incompatible-target success deficit?
Contact-phase aliasing drives the 9-point incompatible deficit; phase-conditioned fingerprints cut it to ≤5 points without retraining residuals.
Reanalyze ManipShift’s nine-point deficit by comparing phase-conditioned and unconditioned fingerprint routing with frozen residuals and residual-only controls.
On ManipShift, phase-conditioned routing reduced incompatible scratch gap from 9 to 4 points with frozen residuals; residual-only gap was 2.
Reconsider fingerprint routing with phase-conditioned fingerprints: incompatible-target scratch gap fell to 4 points; overlap parity remains unverified.
Benchmark revived phase-conditioned routing on 30-seed ManipShift overlap targets at half-budget against full-budget scratch, recording success and interaction counts.
ManipShift phase-routing scorecard logs 30-seed overlap success at half-budget, full-budget scratch success, and target-interaction counts.
ModeStitch composes source contact-mode options using target-calibrated successor features, accepting switches only under conservative advantage over scratch.
ModeStitch matches full-budget scratch success at half-budget on ManipShift overlap targets and trails equal-budget scratch ≤5 points on incompatible targets.
Using ManipShift transfer scorecard’s scratch baselines, benchmark ModeStitch across 30 seeds on half-budget overlap and equal-budget incompatible targets.
On ManipShift, ModeStitch reached 73% half-budget overlap success versus 72% full-budget scratch; incompatible success trailed equal-budget scratch by 3 points.
Prioritize ModeStitch: half-budget overlap exceeds full-budget scratch, and its incompatible gap is 3 points versus phase-routing’s 4.
Does ModeStitch’s conservative switch rule remain reliable when friction shifts mid-episode, invalidating calibrated successor features?
Following ModeStitch prioritization, inject mid-episode friction jumps in ManipShift; measure switch errors, half-budget overlap parity, and equal-budget scratch gap.
On 30-seed ManipShift-Jump, double friction after grasp and compare ModeStitch switch errors and success against static-friction and scratch controls.
ManipShift-Jump audit logs friction-jump timing, option-switch errors, half-budget overlap success, and equal-budget incompatible scratch gaps across 30 seeds.
Check ManipShift-Jump audit against phase-routing scorecard for seed alignment, scratch-baseline consistency, and half-budget interaction accounting.
Seed-aligned, budget-checked ManipShift-Jump audits found 18% erroneous ModeStitch switches and an 8-point incompatible scratch gap, exceeding the 5-point limit.
After the 8-point jump deficit, add online friction-change detection and scratch fallback; rerun ManipShift-Jump to verify ≤5-point gap.
Implement CUSUM friction-change detection with scratch fallback, then rerun 30-seed ManipShift-Jump measuring erroneous switches and equal-budget scratch gaps.
ManipShift-Jump v2 audit adds CUSUM alarm times, scratch-fallback transitions, switch-error rates, and equal-budget success gaps to v1 logs.
Reweight source replay by target transition likelihood for offline policy warm-starts, rejecting mismatched samples and retaining scratch-only updates.
Can target-transition likelihood weighting retain useful source replay while excluding samples that cause negative transfer under hidden dynamics shifts?
On 30-seed ManipShift, compare likelihood-weighted and unweighted replay with scratch, tracking sample retention and half-budget overlap/equal-budget incompatible success.
On ManipShift, weighted replay reached 65% half-budget overlap success versus 72% full-budget scratch; incompatible success lagged scratch by 7 points.
Mode-conditioned replay lifts half-budget overlap success from 65% to ≥72% and cuts incompatible scratch gap from 7 to ≤5 points.
After weighted replay’s 65% overlap success and 7-point incompatible gap, stratify replay by contact mode and retest ManipShift.
Using ManipShift-Jump v2 alarms, filter stale transitions; test mode-stratified replay’s half-budget overlap and equal-budget incompatible success versus scratch.
On 30-seed ManipShift, alarm-filtered mode replay reached 73% half-budget overlap success and a 4-point incompatible scratch gap.
Reconsider replay transfer with alarm-filtered contact-mode weighting: half-budget overlap reached 73%, and incompatible gap fell to 4 points.
After replay revival, test mode-stratified replay on held-out ManipShift latency shifts for half-budget overlap and equal-budget incompatible success.
ManipShift-Latency replay scorecard contains held-out success curves, alarm-filtered replay retention, interaction counts, and scratch comparisons.
Learn factorized source dynamics ensembles, adapt target-specific factors online, and use pessimistic MPC with scratch-policy fallback under disagreement.
Using ManipShift phase-routing and latency-replay scorecards, benchmark factorized-ensemble MPC against both on half-budget overlap and equal-budget incompatible success.
ManipShift MPC reached 75% half-budget overlap success versus 72% full-budget scratch; incompatible success trailed equal-budget scratch by 2 points.
Prioritize factorized-ensemble MPC: 75% half-budget overlap success and 2-point incompatible gap outperform replay’s 73%/4-point and phase-routing’s 4-point gap.
Validate prioritized factorized-ensemble MPC across 50-seed ManipShift-Jump/Latency, checking half-budget overlap parity and ≤5-point equal-budget incompatible gaps.
Run 50-seed ManipShift-Jump/Latency MPC versus scratch, recording overlap half-budget success, incompatible equal-budget gaps, and fallback frequency.
ManipShift robustness report records 50-seed Jump/Latency MPC success curves, scratch baselines, target-interaction budgets, and fallback frequencies.
Audit robustness report for paired seeds, counted calibration interactions, confidence intervals, and Jump/Latency success against both task thresholds.
Budget-corrected 50-seed audit found Jump overlap success 70% versus 72% full-budget scratch; Latency incompatible gap reached 6 points.
Suspend prioritized MPC: budget-corrected Jump overlap trails scratch by 2 points, while Latency incompatibility exceeds the five-point limit.
Do calibration costs explain MPC’s Jump overlap shortfall, while delayed disagreement detection explains its Latency negative transfer?
Reducing calibration to ≤20 interactions restores Jump parity; triggering scratch fallback within three steps reduces Latency gap to ≤5 points.
Using robustness-report seeds, ablate ≤20-interaction calibration and ≤3-step scratch fallback; compare budget-corrected Jump success and Latency scratch gaps.
On ManipShift, 20-interaction/three-step MPC: Jump 71% versus scratch 72%, Latency gap 6 points; bootstrap-gated adapters: Jump 72%, gap 3 points.
Stratify paired robustness-report and ablation runs by calibration cost and fallback delay, comparing Jump/Latency failures against bootstrap-gated adapters.
In ≤20-interaction Jump-overlap strata, MPC matched scratch at 72%; ≤3-step-fallback Latency-incompatible strata showed a 4-point gap.
Keep bootstrap-gated adapters as default: favorable MPC strata meet thresholds, but overall MPC misses Jump parity and Latency safety.
Keep bootstrap-gated adapters default; retest suspended MPC with ≤20-interaction calibration and ≤3-step fallback for half-budget parity and ≤5-point gaps.
Using robustness-report seeds, rerun MPC with ≤20 calibration interactions and ≤3-step fallback across full Jump/Latency cohorts at matched budgets.
ManipShift robustness report v2 adds matched-budget full-cohort Jump/Latency MPC reruns, calibration counts, fallback delays, and scratch comparisons.
Audit v2 calibration charges and fallback timestamps; compare paired 50-seed Jump overlap and Latency incompatible outcomes against scratch.
ManipShift v2 audit: Jump overlap reached 71% versus 72% scratch; Latency incompatible success trailed scratch by 6 points.
Retain bootstrap-gated adapters; full-cohort MPC still misses Jump parity by 1 point and exceeds Latency’s safety limit by 1.
